chunks.text: # File Embedding Search A small Python CLI that extracts text from `.txt` and `.pdf` files, splits it into overlapping chunks, creates OpenAI embeddings, stores them in a local JSON file, and returns the most relevant chunk for a question. ## Setup 1. Create and activate a virtual environment: ```powershell py -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 ``` 2. Install dependencies: ```powershell pip install -r requirements.txt ``` 3. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and add your OpenAI API key. Never commit `.env`. ## Usage Index a text or PDF file: ```powershell python app.py index path\to\document.pdf ``` This writes the embeddings to `data/index.json`, which is ignored by Git. Search the indexed document: ```powershell python app.py search "What is the main topic?" ``` Use a different index location or embedding model with `--store` and `--model`: ```powershell python app.py index notes.txt --store data/notes.json --model text-embedding-3-small python app.py search "Explain the conclusi

-model`: ```powershell python app.py index notes.txt --store data/notes.json --model text-embedding-3-small python app.py search "Explain the conclusion" --store data/notes.json ``` The current search returns the single highest-scoring chunk using cosine similarity. The JSON index is intentionally simple and local; it can later be replaced with a vector database without changing text extraction or chunking. ## Tests ```powershell pytest ``` The tests cover chunking and cosine similarity and do not call the OpenAI API. ## Upload To GitHub Create an empty repository on GitHub, then run: ```powershell git add . git commit -m "Build file embedding search CLI" git branch -M main git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/YOUR-REPOSITORY.git git push -u origin main ```
